definition: Soft robotics is a subfield of robotics that concerns the design, control, and fabrication of robots composed of compliant materials, instead of rigid links.
details: In contrast to rigid-bodied robots built from metals, ceramics and hard plastics, the compliance of soft robots can improve their safety when working in close contact with humans.

explainer.lead: Soft robotics is the design, control, and fabrication of robots made from compliant materials instead of rigid links. Its compliance can improve safety when robots work in close contact with humans.

tiers.eli5: These robots are squishy rather than stiff, so bumping into one is more like bumping into a soft toy than a machine.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fabricate bodies from compliant materials rather than metals, ceramics, or hard plastics. The pitfall is control: soft bodies deform in complex ways, making them harder to model and command precisely than rigid-link robots.
tiers.paperLevel: Soft robotics concerns robots composed of compliant materials rather than rigid links, covering their design, control, and fabrication. Known limit: compliance improves safety in close human contact but complicates precise control relative to rigid-bodied robots.

explainer.example: A compliant robotic gripper made of soft material picks up an object and conforms to its shape, reducing the risk of damage or injury during contact.
